documents.unit: Center for the Advancement of Teaching
documents.title: Sample Syllabus Statements for the Use of AI Tools in Your Course
documents.stance_why: The document supplies sample statements (permitted/limited, 'Use Encouraged and Permitted', 'Use Prohibited') and says to 'adjust the guidance to fit your particular context'. It sets no single rule and hands the choice to instructors, so delegates with tiers.
tiers: Acceptable and Unacceptable Use of AI (limited)
documents.summary: Teaching-center templates that instructors adapt for syllabi, covering limited use, encouraged use and full prohibition. Each template stresses documentation, responsibility for output, and instructor-chosen penalties.

units.why: The sample statements are offered for instructors to adapt: 'adjust the guidance to fit your particular context'. The decision rests with each instructor, so actor is instructor, phase before-course, and P04.
units.anchor: adjust the guidance to fit your particular context

units.why: Instructors are told to 'note in specific assignment descriptions where AI use is allowed or disallowed', which is a duty to state AI expectations at assignment level, so P09 for instructors at course-start.
units.anchor: note in specific assignment descriptions where AI use is allowed or disallowed

units.why: The document offers three templates (acceptable/unacceptable, encouraged, prohibited). 'allowing the use of AI tools for certain purposes, but not for others' describes a middle tier; naming the tiers is P05.
units.anchor: allowing the use of AI tools for certain purposes, but not for others

units.why: The sample permits AI for 'Brainstorming and refining your ideas', which is a brainstorming permission (P15) addressed to students during work.
units.anchor: Brainstorming and refining your ideas

units.why: Permitting AI for 'Finding information on your topic' treats AI like a search tool for understanding a topic, not producing graded answers, so P12.
units.anchor: Finding information on your topic

units.why: Fine tuning research questions is a permitted use of AI in refining one's own thinking; it is closest to brainstorming and exploring approaches, P15, rather than tutoring.
units.anchor: Fine tuning your research questions
units.fit_note: Refining research questions is idea development with AI, a little beyond brainstorming.

units.why: 'Drafting an outline to organize your thoughts' is a permitted writing-support use, i.e. P91 (outlining and organizing).
units.anchor: Drafting an outline to organize your thoughts

units.why: 'Checking grammar and style' is permitted, a writing-support use, so P91.
units.anchor: Checking grammar and style

units.why: The sample forbids 'Impersonating you in classroom contexts', such as composing discussion board posts or Zoom chat content. P58 (students write their own course communication) is nearest, though it covers messages to staff rather than posts to peers.
units.anchor: Impersonating you in classroom contexts
units.fit_note: Covers discussion board and Zoom chat contributions, not only messages to course staff.

units.why: The sample bars AI from 'Completing group work that your group has assigned to you' unless the group agrees. No type covers group-agreed AI use, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Completing group work that your group has assigned to you
units.uncovered_note: AI may not do one's assigned share of group work unless the group mutually agrees to its use.

units.why: 'Writing a draft of a writing assignment' is listed as not permitted, i.e. AI may not produce the work submitted, P19.
units.anchor: Writing a draft of a writing assignment

units.why: 'Writing entire sentences, paragraphs or papers to complete class assignments' is prohibited: AI must not produce submitted text, P19.
units.anchor: Writing entire sentences, paragraphs or papers to complete class assignments

units.why: 'You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query' makes the student answerable for submitted content, P29 (the examples about IP and misinformation are secondary).
units.anchor: You are responsible for the information you submit based on an AI query

units.why: 'Your use of AI tools must be properly documented and cited' is a disclosure duty with each submission, P24, tied to academic honesty.
units.anchor: must be properly documented and cited

units.why: The statement tells instructors to insert a penalty for unauthorized AI use: 'found to have used generative AI tools in unauthorized ways [insert the penalty here*]'. Stating penalties in advance is P37.
units.anchor: found to have used generative AI tools in unauthorized ways

units.why: 'When in doubt about permitted usage, please ask for clarification' tells students to ask before using AI, P10.
units.anchor: When in doubt about permitted usage, please ask for clarification

units.why: The encouraged template says students are 'welcome/expected to use generative AI tools', a permit/encourage default for the course, P02 (which covers 'expects').
units.anchor: You are welcome/expected to use generative AI tools

units.why: The template ties AI use to a course goal: 'aligns with the course learning goal [insert...]'. Basing AI permission on learning objectives is P83.
units.anchor: aligns with the course learning goal

units.why: The prohibited template says generative AI tools 'are not permitted in this class', a ban on all AI use for the course, P01.
units.anchor: are not permitted in this class

units.why: Under the prohibited template use 'may be considered a violation of Temple University's Academic Honesty policy and Student Conduct Code', i.e. misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: may be considered a violation of Temple University’s Academic Honesty policy and Student Conduct Code

units.why: 'The use of unauthorized AI tools will result in [insert the penalty here*]' calls for a stated penalty in the syllabus, P37.
units.anchor: The use of unauthorized AI tools will result in

units.why: The footnote recommends 'conversations in your department about the appropriate penalties', with different levels for first-time and repeat offenders. This is escalation by offense (P37) but also a department-level deliberation the type does not mention.
units.anchor: appropriate level of penalty for first-time offenders and those who repeatedly violate
units.frag_end: violate your policies on the use of AI.
units.fit_note: Recommends departmental discussion of penalty levels rather than stating penalties.

documents.title: Generative AI and Chatbots (research guide)
documents.stance_why: Mostly advice, but the one rule it states is 'Temple policy prohibits the use of generative AI tools in a class, unless the instructor explicitly grants permission'. Ban unless explicitly permitted is restrict.
documents.summary: A library guide that supports AI exploration and teaches how chatbots work. It reports the university default that AI is prohibited in class unless the instructor permits it, with unauthorized use treated as misconduct.

units.why: 'Temple policy prohibits the use of generative AI tools in a class, unless the instructor explicitly grants permission' sets a university default ban with explicit permission as the exception, so P06 (fallback when syllabus silent) fits best over P01 since permission by instructors is the stated exception.
units.anchor: prohibits the use of generative AI tools in a class, unless the instructor explicitly

units.why: 'Temple's Student Code of Conduct defines unauthorized use of generative AI as academic misconduct' classifies misuse as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: defines unauthorized use of generative AI as academic misconduct

units.why: 'Different instructors may have different rules related to the use of generative AI' says the rule varies by instructor, P04.
units.anchor: Different instructors may have different rules related to the use of generative AI

units.why: 'Students should read their syllabi carefully to learn what is permitted in a class' makes students responsible for learning each course's rules, P78.
units.anchor: Students should read their syllabi carefully to learn what is permitted in a class

units.why: 'We encourage you to test out AI tools and chatbots' is the Libraries' invitation to experiment; it encourages use but is not a course rule, so P02 with a fit note.
units.anchor: We encourage you to test out AI tools and chatbots
units.fit_note: A library invitation to explore tools, not a default rule for graded work (and in tension with the class ban stated below).

units.why: The self-paced tutorial teaches how chatbots work and their strengths and weaknesses, so it is AI-literacy training for users, P70.
units.anchor: describe how chatbots work, identify strengths and weaknesses of current chatbots

units.why: 'Make an appointment with a subject librarian or specialist' and the Ask a Librarian line direct users to human help, P72.
units.anchor: Make an appointment

notes: Two included documents only. Coder A. Syllabus PDF text is one word per line; anchors checked by validator.
